beats.say: Standing tickets jump price while you wait.
Early bird promises a spot at the listed price.
Regular option offers the same seat later, no guarantee.
Premium tag says 'in demand' and hints at higher cost.
First shows £148.50, then £355. Looks like a mistake.
But it does a queue trick: surge pricing.
Ticketmaster raises the 'in demand' tag after hours in line.
The surge climbs from £148.50 to £355 because waiting time fuels demand.
The CMA opened an investigation, confirming the shift is deliberate.
A cinema lists standard seats £10, premium £12, and a 'high demand' slot £20.
The high-demand slot feels worth it because the jump mirrors the concert trick.
